items.problem: For an input command that ends by its time limit (line 40) while it still has device inputs to put in, the spec does not set whether QACore stops putting them in and releases what it holds. Line 41 covers only the operation the command waits for (content command handler, operation of another module), and line 128 sets "an ended command puts in no device input after that" and the release of held touches, keys, mouse buttons and gamepad buttons only for a connection drop. Run path: `text` puts in one character per frame with limit `QACore.commandTimeoutMs` only (line 40, line 65), so a `text` of `QACore.textMaxChars` characters whose frames take longer than the limit (or a `drag`/`key` whose frames stall past `QACore.commandTimeoutMs` + ms) ends with `ok` = `false`; one implementation keeps putting in the remaining characters or the pending move/release after the response, another stops and leaves the touch or key pressed, so the next `tap` takes another touch index and `touch_down` of that index fails differently per implementation

What QACore's own remaining work does after a command ends by its time limit is not set, while it is set for a connection drop (qa-core.md:128) and `release` (qa-core.md:250). The new rule at qa-core.md:41 covers only a late end of the operation the command waits for (content handler, another module's operation), not QACore's own work. Reproducing input: game settings `QACore.textMaxChars` (owner content) 1000 and `QACore.commandTimeoutMs` 10000 at 60 FPS; `text` of 1000 characters puts in one text input per frame (qa-core.md:65), so it reaches the time limit after about 600 characters. One implementation stops putting in text inputs, another keeps putting them in after the `ok` = `false` response, so the text field content after the command differs. Likewise a `tap` whose release frame comes after the limit (a frame longer than `QACore.commandTimeoutMs`) can leave the touch index pressed or release it, which changes the touch index the next `tap` uses (qa-core.md:120), and a `capture_video` that reaches its limit can send frame messages after the response or stop, against qa-core.md:125. These rules predate the change range
